title: Naive-Student: Leveraging Semi-Supervised Learning in Video Sequences for Urban Scene Segmentation
mechanism: An offline teacher with multi-scale and flip TTA pseudo-labels a large pool (hard labels, no threshold). The student trains on the pseudo-labels only, is then fine-tuned on the human labels, and the loop is repeated.
adaptation: Teacher = 5-seed PF ensemble with 8 dihedral TTA (flips and rot90 are label-safe), labelling the 11.9k CSIR/ARTS pool and later 159k. Store soft p(crack) and p(inactive); use argmax plus the val-chosen crack bias for the other classes. Student = house U-Net++ R34 (and a wider encoder): 40k steps on the pseudo-labelled pool with strong aug, then 20k PF fine-tune on the 478 labelled cells. It differs from our Mean Teacher in the offline, stronger teacher, the pseudo-only pretraining and the larger pool.
min_experiment: Arm NS-12k vs house PF (5 seeds each). Metrics: clean-49 crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if crack IoU gains less than 0.012 and E1 relF1@2 gains less than 0.03. If it survives, rerun with the 159k pool.
evidence: R: full Cityscapes labels (2,975), 89k video frames + 20k extra unlabelled. Student 82.5 -> 85.7 mIoU (+3.2) at iteration 1, +0.8 at iteration 2. Teacher used multi-scale + flip TTA.
prior_overlap: BRIEF row 'Pseudo-label SSL' tested an online EMA Mean Teacher (same R34) with hard/tolerant pseudo-labels at 100% labels and the 11.9k pool: n.d. Not tested: an offline ensemble+TTA teacher, pseudo-only pretraining then fine-tune, the 159k pool, or model distillation (listed as never tried). Still open.
